body:
Ava: kicked off evaluation for Mercury customer finetune with synthetic casebook. quick note — we ran int4 and int8 passes against the standard eval set and a new synthetic 'legal-casebook' set.
Diego: any initial surprises?
Ava: int4 looked largely OK on factual recall but hallucination on date normalization spiked on the synthetic set.
Priya: can you paste the top diff? :thinking_face:
Ava: here's the distilled diff for answer types (short):
```
metric | base-int8 | finetune-int4
EM     | 0.82      | 0.79
F1     | 0.85      | 0.82
Halluc | 0.03      | 0.09
```
Sam: 6% absolute hallucination jump is non-trivial. Did we keep the same tokenizer/merging method for LoRA?
Ava: yes same tokenizer, LoRA merged with stitched keys; we used the adapter-stitch script v2 and kept vocab intact. Command:
```
python tools/merge_adapter.py --base mercury-base --lora finetune-lora --out merged/mercury-v2
```
Priya: sounds like int4 kernel path might be dropping some normalization tokens. Can infra rerun KV-cache warmstart with debug logging?
infra-bot: New job queued: kv-warmstart-debug (id: job-4829). Estimated run: 8m.
Diego: also let's run a small prompt set where dates are formatted variably (e.g., 'Jan 2, 2020', '2/1/20', '2020-01-02') to replicate the spike.
Ava: starting that now against merged/mercury-v2 int4. I'll post raw examples + model outputs when done.
Priya: if confirmed, plan: 1) try quant-aware calibration using representative prompt set, 2) try small-scale 8-bit fallback for date-sensitive routes, 3) add a quick eval to the customer's smokepack monitoring.
Sam: agree. Also add a canary route with auto-fallback to int8 when hallucination confidence low.
Ava: noted. Action items: @Diego check tokenizer bit-level equality, @Priya run calibration, @Sam update routing policy, @infra-bot attach run logs. ETA EOD.
Diego: on it, will report by 16:30 PT.
Ava: thanks — attaching a short sample in thread when kv job finishes. :thumbsup:
